title: Finite constant ordinary modules have finite presentations after the common encoding
statement: Let $B$ be a finite discrete commutative topological ring, let $T$ be any scheme, and fix the monoidal constant-ring identification $e$ and the equivalence $G$ with its specified equality of underlying additive-group functors as in [def-weil-pbc-common-finite-discrete-encoding]. Write $E_T$ for that particular sectionwise encoding from sheaves of $\operatorname{ULift}B$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] to internal modules over $R_T=p_T^*C(-,B)$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. If $P$ is a $\operatorname{ULift}B$-module whose underlying set is finite and $\underline P_T$ is its constant sheaf on $T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], then $E_T(\underline P_T)$ is finitely presented as an internal $R_T$-module [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. Explicitly, there are $m,n\in\mathbf N$ and an internal $R_T$-linear map $d:R_T^m\to R_T^n$ such that $E_T(\underline P_T)\cong\operatorname{coker}(d)$, where $R_T^k$ is the finite sum of $k$ regular modules. The assertion holds for the empty scheme and the zero ring, and imposes no Noetherian hypothesis on $T$.
